_doc: Experiments shown on the Experiments page (beta/tournaments_page.py, beta/tournaments.html; the page was named Tournaments
until 2026-11-25, and each series on it was "Tournament N"); the home page
(beta/home_rankings.py, beta/landing.html) carried them as a table until 2026-11-21.
Each runs from its first game (`start`, a run tag; every game with a later tag
that matches `match` counts) in series of `series_size` finished games, read off
the ledger's results.jsonl at publish time. A game's best run counts once; a
launch that never reached a board (outcome unfinished) is not a game.
An optional `end` (a run tag) closes a definition: only games whose tag sorts before it count.
An optional `note` is shown in the table's Notes column on every series of its definition.
Operator /goal 2026-11-19 ~18:35Z: repeated 10-game series against Lv 8 Deity AI,
6P Continents; conditions Lv 8 6P Continents Online.
Operator 2026-11-19 ~21:20Z: "Turn the ongoing tournament into a 100 game tournament": Tournament 1 stays the
first 10-game series; from Tournament 2's first game (civvis-20261119T204058Z) the series are 100 games.
Operator ~21:30Z: "actually lets just do 30 games for now, rather than 100": series of 30.
Operator ~22:45Z: "we should randomly choose a civ. but then we should pursue our top strategy for winning, given the civ" and
"lets restart the tournament with this in mind. best of 30 games": Tournament 2 closes at civvis-20261119T223800Z (a series cut short by
its definition's `end` still gets an end date); Tournament 3 is a new 30-game series from there.
Operator 2026-11-20 ~01:40Z: "tournament 2 was scraped. (can add a notes col). both civs and strategies were being
chosen at random (random strat among the top ~5 or so I think). but what should be done is picking a civ at random
and then picking our best strategy for the civ. should be fixed in tournament 3. unsure if tournament 1 is affected
(probably is).": the `note` on each definition.
Operator 2026-11-20 ~05:50Z: "make the ongoing tournament a 100 game tourney please. continue the existing games series":
Tournament 3 stays the best-of-30 that ended at civvis-20261120T045254Z; Tournament 4 keeps its games from there as a 100-game series.
Operator 2026-11-21 ~02:35Z: "finish off the 50 game tournament please. make the video": the 100-game definition becomes 50-game series,
so Tournament 4 is its first 50 games (through civvis-20261120T150010Z) and Tournament 5 continues from the next.
Operator 2026-11-21 ~05:20Z: "have tournament 6 be: 10 games on lv 4, 10 games on lv 5, 10 games on lv 6, 10 games on lv 7, 10 games
on lv 8. 6p continents. 2 civvis agents and 4 deity ais ... start automatically once you finish the current tournament"; whole game
at that level, a game is a win when either CIVVIS agent wins. Those games are hotseat tables tagged `civvis-t6-<utc>`, so the
single-seat 50-game definition ends at "civvis-t" (every `civvis-2026...` tag sorts before it) and the table owns its own prefix.
Operator 2026-11-21 ~05:35Z: "Between Home and CIVVIS, we want to add a Tournaments view. This is my Simulator Experiments page
essentially. I have an idea I want to run. I schedule in a tournament for it. The AI models just keep working away at games.":
scheduling a tournament is adding its definition to this list. A definition none of whose games has finished is listed on the
Tournaments page as scheduled, in the order of this list, numbered on from the last tournament begun. One that is to wait its turn
owns a tag prefix (`civvis-t7-`), as Tournament 6 does, so it can be defined before the games ahead of it are played.
An optional `idea` says in a sentence what the tournament tests; the page shows it under the tournament's name.
Operator 2026-11-21 ~07:00Z: "on our new tournaments page we are building out. we can link to the youtube tournament result videos.":
`videos` names a tournament's result video on the CIVVIS YouTube channel, by the tournament's number as the page shows it (a
definition played as repeated series is several tournaments, so the link cannot sit on a definition). The page links it under the
tournament's name. The operator posts the videos; add a line here when one is up. Only a YouTube watch link is linked.
Operator 2026-11-21 ~14:50Z: "for tournament 6, lets cut back to 5 games at each level (5 on lv 4... 5 on lv 8)": 25 games.
Operator 2026-11-21 ~20:35Z: "for each tournament, we should have a short description. T1: Proof of concept, 10 game series.
T2: Abandoned. T3: 30 game series. T4: 50 game series T5: Repeat 50 game series but with 2/6 CIVVIS AI Agents (2nd half no
Diplo allowed). T6: Benchmarking across levels: 5 games at each level (no Diplo allowed). the descriptions can be on the title
line. please make title line bigger too.": `descriptions` gives a tournament's short description, by the tournament's number
as the page shows it, like `videos` and for the same reason (Tournaments 4 and 5 are one definition). The page writes it on the
tournament's title line, "Tournament 4: 50 game series". They are the operator's words; every tournament has one, so add a
line here when a tournament is scheduled or begins. A definition may carry its own `description` instead, which is used when
`descriptions` has no line for its number (a scheduled tournament's number can move if the queue is reordered).
Operator 2026-11-21 ~20:38Z: "for tournament 6 we should just have 1 of our civvis in the game. other 5 are ai. please restart
tournament 6" and "no diplo allowed for any level": Tournament 6 starts again at the first table tagged after the restart
(`start` is that moment as a table tag), one CIVVIS agent and five Firaxis AI, the Diplomatic victory switched off in every game.
The first attempt's games (two CIVVIS agents; civvis-t6-20261121T131243Z, a win, and one table never finished) sort before
`start` and count in no tournament.
Operator 2026-11-22 ~04:50Z: "please add an indefinite tourney - whenever we have no other tourney, we run lv 6, lv 7, lv 8
(x 2) games. diplomacy off. benchmark our win rates roughly for these games over time.": a definition with `indefinite`
is one series that never fills (no `series_size`); its `end` only bounds the tags it counts, so a tournament played between
its games pauses it and does not close it. The page shows its win rate by level, over every game and day by day. Its games
are tagged `civvis-t7-` and played in turn at Lv 6, Lv 7, Lv 8, Lv 8 by the host's conductor whenever no other tournament
is being played.
Operator 2026-11-23 ~04:10Z: "across lv 4 - 8, lets run the autotourney (the indefinite one) to play games 1/8 chance on lv 4,
5, 6, 7 and 1/2 chance on level 8 ... this will be our primary Firaxis Civ 6 AI benchmark - win rate on each level. half the
games can be diplo, half no diplo.": the same tournament (its tags, `start` and `end` are unchanged), dealt differently from
2026-11-23 ~04:30Z. The host's conductor deals the games in blocks of 16, each block Lv 8 eight times and Lv 4, 5, 6 and 7
twice each, half of every level's games with the Diplomatic victory on and half with it off, in an order shuffled per block.
A game's result line does not say which; its run summary on the ledger does (`seat.victories`), and Win Analytics
(beta/research_page.py) lists the two kinds of game in two tables, Diplomatic off and Diplomatic allowed.
Operator 2026-11-23: "please spell out the tourney hyperparameters for each tourney clearly": `hyperparameters` lists, by the
tournament's number as `descriptions` and `videos` do (Tournaments 4 and 5 are one definition), every setting its games were
played under: Games, AI level, Players, Victory types, Civ, Strategy, Map, Game speed, Turn limit, Ruleset, Played in, Game end
and CIVVIS agent, in that order (`tournaments_page.HYPERPARAMETERS`). Tournaments 1-7's were read back from their games' run
summaries on the ledger (`seat`, `map_size`, `speed`, `max_turns`, `ruleset`, `victories`, `decider_revisions`) on 2026-11-23.
Add a tournament's line when it is scheduled; a definition may carry its own `hyperparameters`, used for a number with no line.
Operator 2026-11-23 ~20:50Z: "Call our Indefinite Tourney the "Indefinite Benchmarking Tourney". Runs games for
benchmarking. Can run analytics over the games. Track progress over time. When we have a Tournament to run, we can pause the
Indefinite Benchmarking and run the specific Tournament. Then back to benchmarking tourneys. We should use opus 5.5 to try
to spot problem we make in benchmarking games, fix the problems in code and self-imrpove our performance over time.":
Tournament 7 is the Indefinite Benchmarking Tourney (its `descriptions` line, the page's title line). A scheduled tournament
pauses it: the host's bench conductor yields while another tournament's conductor has its policy block in, that tournament
plays under its own tag prefix, and the benchmark resumes when it is done. Each finished benchmark game is read by Claude
Opus 5.5 on the host (bench/review_bench.py), which lists the mistakes it finds; a mistake seen in several games is handed
to an Opus 5.5 session that fixes it in code as an opt-in gene, ships it and arms it, and the benchmark's win rates measure
the change.
Operator 2026-11-25 ~05:40Z: "REplace tournament with experiment inside experiments/. that is really what they are. isn't
about winning. trying to learn.": each series is "Experiment N" on the page.
Operator 2026-11-25 ~05:50Z: "put the experiments list on the left 60%. the scheduled games & benchmark can be on the right.
tourney 7 is benchmark. please remove from experiments and make the official benchmark for now": the definition marked
`benchmark` is not an experiment. The page draws it on its own, as the Official Benchmark, in the right-hand column under
Scheduled, and numbers the experiments without it, so the next one scheduled is Experiment 7. A number in `descriptions`,
`videos` and `hyperparameters` is an experiment's number; the benchmark carries its own `description` and
`hyperparameters` on its definition. Its tags (`civvis-t7-`) and the host's bench conductor are unchanged.
Operator 2026-11-26: "please add a tournament with 100 lv 8 deity games, no diplo. lets really work on the self improvement
and optimization of the algorithm. our victory rate here should be much higher.": Experiment 7, the definition after the
benchmark's, is 100 games at Lv 8 Deity, one CIVVIS agent and five Firaxis AI on Continents, the Diplomatic victory off in
every game. Its games are tagged `civvis-t8-` (the benchmark's `end`, so none of them counts in the benchmark) and the host's
conductor plays them from the moment it was scheduled, pausing the benchmark until 100 have finished. Unlike the benchmark,
the conductor picks each game's victory lane by Thompson sampling over Religious, Science and Culture, on the results of every
Lv 8 Diplomatic-off game in each lane (the benchmark's and the experiment's), so the lane that wins is played more, and then
draws the civ among the civs suited to that lane. The newest build plays each game; Claude Opus 5.5 reviews every one, as it
does the benchmark's, and a mistake that recurs is fixed in code as a gene and armed, so the agent improves during the experiment.

descriptions.5: Repeat 50 game series but with 2/6 CIVVIS AI Agents (2nd half no Diplo allowed)
descriptions.6: Benchmarking across levels: 5 games at each level (no Diplo allowed)
descriptions.7: 100 Lv 8 Deity games, no Diplo allowed

1.Victory types: All six: Science, Culture, Domination, Religious, Diplomatic, Score
1.Strategy: Probably random among our top ~5, as in Experiment 2 (unconfirmed)
1.Map: Continents, Small, 9 city-states, a new map each game
1.Game end: Games 1-2 conceded early by restart rules (an early city lost; science out of reach), switched off from game 3; games 3-10 played out: a victory, our elimination or turn 250
1.CIVVIS agent: The newest build when each game launched: 4 builds over 10 games

2.Victory types: All six: Science, Culture, Domination, Religious, Diplomatic, Score
2.Strategy: Random among our top ~5 (the reason it was scrapped)
2.Map: Continents, Small, 9 city-states, a new map each game
2.Game end: Played out: a victory, our elimination or turn 250
2.CIVVIS agent: The newest build when each game launched: 2 builds over 11 games

3.Victory types: All six: Science, Culture, Domination, Religious, Diplomatic, Score
3.Strategy: Our best strategy for the civ drawn
3.Map: Continents, Small, 9 city-states, a new map each game
3.Game end: Played out: a victory, our elimination or turn 250
3.CIVVIS agent: The newest build when each game launched: 14 builds over 30 games

4.Victory types: All six: Science, Culture, Domination, Religious, Diplomatic, Score
4.Strategy: Our best strategy for the civ drawn
4.Map: Continents, Small, 9 city-states, a new map each game
4.Game end: Played out: a victory, our elimination or turn 250
4.CIVVIS agent: The newest build when each game launched: 15 builds over 50 games

5.Games: 50 planned; ended at 49 when Experiment 6 began
5.Players: 6: 1 CIVVIS agent + 5 Firaxis AI (the ledger has one CIVVIS civ in each of the 49 games)
5.Victory types: Games 1-25: all six (Science, Culture, Domination, Religious, Diplomatic, Score). Games 26-49: all but Diplomatic
5.Strategy: Our best strategy for the civ drawn
5.Map: Continents, Small, 9 city-states, a new map each game
5.Game end: Played out: a victory, our elimination or turn 250
5.CIVVIS agent: The newest build when each game launched: 20 builds over 49 games

6.AI level: Lv 4 Prince, Lv 5 King, Lv 6 Emperor, Lv 7 Immortal, Lv 8 Deity: 5 games each, lowest level first
6.Victory types: All but Diplomatic: Science, Culture, Domination, Religious, Score
6.Strategy: Our best strategy for the civ drawn
6.Map: Continents, Small, 9 city-states, a new map each game
6.Played in: Civ VI hotseat for games 1-7, single player from game 8
6.Game end: Played out: a victory, our elimination or turn 250
6.CIVVIS agent: The newest build when each game launched: 6 builds over games 8-25

7.Victory types: All but Diplomatic: Science, Culture, Domination, Religious, Score
7.Civ: Random each game, among the civs suited to the victory lane chosen for it
7.Strategy: The victory lane is chosen each game by Thompson sampling over Religious, Science and Culture, on the results of every Lv 8 Diplomatic-off game in each lane (the benchmark's and this experiment's), so the lane that wins is played more. On the ledger when it was scheduled: Religious 3 wins in 29 benchmark games, Science 0 in 68, Culture never played
7.Map: Continents, Small, 9 city-states, a new map each game
7.Game end: Played out: a victory, our elimination or turn 250
7.CIVVIS agent: The newest build when each game launched; Claude Opus 5.5 reviews every game, and a mistake it finds in several games is fixed in code as a gene and armed, so the agent improves during the experiment

tournaments.name: Lv 4 to Lv 8 against the Firaxis AI, 1 CIVVIS agent + 5 AI
tournaments.idea: Benchmark games, played whenever no experiment is: one CIVVIS agent against five Firaxis AI, half the games at Lv 8 and an eighth at each of Lv 4, 5, 6 and 7, half of each level's games with the Diplomatic victory allowed. A scheduled experiment pauses it, and it resumes when that experiment is done. Its win rate at each level is our primary benchmark against the Firaxis AI, tracked over time here and on Win Analytics. Claude Opus 5.5 reviews every game for our mistakes, and a mistake that recurs is fixed in code, so the agent improves as the benchmark runs.

tournaments.name: Lv 8 Deity, Diplomatic victory off, 100 games
tournaments.idea: One hundred games against the Lv 8 Deity AI with the Diplomatic victory off, to raise our Deity win rate: each game's victory lane is picked by Thompson sampling over Religious, Science and Culture, so the lane that wins is played more, and the civ is drawn among those suited to it. Claude Opus 5.5 reviews every game, and a mistake that recurs is fixed in code, so the agent improves as the experiment runs.
